note: Thin ad-hoc reference the agents construct. Distinct entries for alarm-state, anomaly, fault, concern and cause, so the ontological cognate (alarm vs anomaly) and the two pins bind apart. The NMOP-native concepts (symptom, problem, incident, confidence) have NO entry and remain residual.

entries.label: resource
entries.example: a router, session, server, or container

entries.label: event
entries.definition: A raw event on a resource at a moment, before interpretation.

entries.label: alarm
entries.definition: A declared undesirable STATE requiring attention.
entries.example: a raised alarm on a resource

entries.label: fault
entries.definition: A confirmed fault occurrence - the thing that has actually gone wrong.
entries.example: a session down; a failed fan

entries.label: anomaly
entries.definition: A deviation from expected behaviour that MAY be benign; not itself an undesirable state.
entries.example: a rising trend that may be expected load

entries.label: concern score
entries.definition: A dynamic concern score annotating an anomaly, recomputed from context; not a fixed severity.

entries.label: cause
entries.definition: A cause derived by correlating events and anomalies; not a static code.
